import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 21

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/21](https://www.erdosproblems.com/21)
- [BaWa21] J. Barát and I. M. Wanless, Intersecting and 2-intersecting hypergraphs with maximal
  covering number: the Erdős-Lovász theme revisited. J. Combin. Des. (2021), 260-286.
- [ErLo75] Erdős, P. and Lovász, L., Problems and results on {$3$}-chromatic hypergraphs and some
  related questions. (1975), 609--627.
- [Ka92b] Kahn, Jeff, On a problem of Erdős and Lovász: random lines in a projective plane.
  Combinatorica (1992), 417-423.
- [Ka94] Kahn, Jeff, On a problem of Erdős and Lovász. II. {$n(r)=O(r)$}. J. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1994), 125-143.
- [Tr14] A. Tripathi, A result on intersecting families with maximum transversal size.
  arXiv:1409.4610 (2014).
-/

namespace Erdos21

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that there is an intersecting family $\mathcal{F}$ of sets of size $n$
(so $A\cap B\neq\emptyset$ for all $A,B\in \mathcal{F}$) with $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=f(n)$ such
that any set $S$ with $\lvert S\rvert \leq n-1$ is disjoint from at least one $A\in \mathcal{F}$. Is
it true that
$$f(n) \ll n?$$

This problem was solved by Kahn [Ka94] who proved the upper bound $f(n) \ll n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_21 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r →
    (Hypergraph.minIntersectingEdges r : ENNReal) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r) := by
  sorry

end Erdos21

findings.description: The [BaWa21] bibliography entry at lines 24–25 lists J. Barát and I. M. Wanless as authors and gives pages 260–286. The paper with the stated title is by János Barát alone and appears in Journal of Combinatorial Designs 29(3) (2021), 193–209. This is a reference-only error; it does not affect the theorem.
findings.source_evidence: The author and journal reference at https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.04444 identify János Barát and pages 193–209. The publisher's Crossref record, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/jcd.21763, independently confirms the title, sole author, volume 29, issue 3, and pages 193–209. The incorrect citation also appears at https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/BaWa21.
findings.suggested_fix: For the title currently cited, replace the bibliographic data with: J. Barát, Intersecting and 2-intersecting hypergraphs with maximal covering number: the Erdős–Lovász theme revisited. J. Combin. Des. 29 (2021), 193–209. DOI: 10.1002/jcd.21763.

reformulations.difference: The helper uses existence of a transversal of size at most r together with nonexistence of one of size at most r−1, rather than the source's condition that every set of size at most r−1 is disjoint from some edge.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Negating HasFiniteTransversal (r−1) gives exactly the source's universally quantified disjointness condition. Applying that condition to the empty set ensures that the family is nonempty. Any edge of a nonempty intersecting r-uniform family is itself a transversal of size r, so the additional HasFiniteTransversal r condition is redundant. The predicate equivalence is proved independently as Review21.admissibility_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean requires one positive constant C satisfying the linear bound for every r≥1, whereas the source uses the asymptotic notation f(r) ≪ r.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every r≥1, all r-subsets of a (2r−1)-element ground set form an admissible family, so the minimum is finite. Consequently an eventual linear bound extends to all positive r by increasing its constant to absorb finitely many initial values. Conversely, a bound for every positive r is an eventual bound. The ENat-to-ENNReal coercion preserves these finite values, and ofReal does not truncate the nonnegative quantity C*r. Review21.theorem_rhs_iff_bigO proves the exact equivalence of the theorem's right-hand side with the usual real-valued Big-O statement; its required finiteness result is also proved in the scratch file.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. Restricting to finite families on Fin n loses nothing: the original paper explicitly considers finite hypergraphs, whose finite vertex unions can be relabeled. Independent Lean checks establish minIntersectingEdges 0 = ⊤ (correctly excluded by 1 ≤ r), minIntersectingEdges 1 = 1, and finiteness for every positive r. Computations also check empty cases, the triangle, and a six-edge 3-uniform example. Both scratch files compile without errors or warnings, and the equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. The positive answer and research solved category agree with the source.
